  {Numbers as strings of bits: representation, the six operators, the classic tricks, popcount, XOR and masks as sets.}

\begin{dpjourney}
\dpstep{1}{Binary Representation}{Bases and conversions $\cdot$ Reading the bits of a number $\cdot$ Fixed width: complement and reversal $\cdot$ Signed integers and overflow $\cdot$ Binary strings as numbers}{Beginner -- 1200}{no}
\dpstep{2}{Bitwise Operators and Their Algebra}{Test, set, clear and toggle $\cdot$ Shifts $\cdot$ Identities between arithmetic and bitwise operators $\cdot$ Operators over a range of numbers $\cdot$ Choosing a number under bitwise constraints}{CF 800 -- 1500}{no}
\dpstep{3}{Classic Bit Tricks}{Powers of two $\cdot$ The lowest set bit and carries $\cdot$ Highest and lowest bit positions}{CF 900 -- 1500}{no}
\dpstep{4}{Counting Bits and Parity}{Popcount $\cdot$ Hamming distance $\cdot$ Set bits over a range of numbers $\cdot$ Counts per bit position}{CF 900 -- 1600}{no}
\dpstep{5}{XOR Fundamentals}{XOR of a range of integers $\cdot$ Undoing XOR $\cdot$ XOR equations on neighbours $\cdot$ XOR of pairs and triplets $\cdot$ Cancellation arguments}{CF 900 -- 1700}{no}

\dppartgoals{
  \item read and write numbers in binary, hexadecimal and two\textquotesingle s complement, and know every width and overflow trap;
  \item use AND, OR, XOR, NOT and shifts fluently, with their algebraic identities and precedence pitfalls;
  \item apply the classic tricks: powers of two, lowest and highest set bit, popcount, parity, XOR cancellation;
  \item represent sets of up to 64 elements as integers and enumerate all subsets.
}
